Anya: ran a quick fault-injection sim against the offload/evict path (local allocator + staged host backing). 95p latency jumps when staging window <= 128MB :grimace:
Sam: can you paste the exact command/config you used?
Anya: sure. short snippet:```./sim --workload=chatty --tenants=50 --staging-threshold=128M --evict-policy=soft-windup --inject-fault=hostpage-delay=15ms```
Olivia: nice, thanks. what's the metric that spikes — tail gen latency or queueing?
Anya: tail gen; tokens/sec steady but P95/P99 climb. CPU scheduling/backpressure shows microbursts when hostpages are requested.
Mike: any evidence it's fragmentation vs host I/O latency?
Anya: both. higher frag ratio means more page requests per op; and if hostpage latency stacks you get queuing into the batcher.
Devon: did you try increasing KV prefix caching or enabling eager prefetch for hot slices?
Anya: tried KV cache bump -> helps P50 but not P99. eager prefetch helps P99 but increases average GPU memory and cost.
Sam: can you run a quick config sweep for: (a) prefetch on, (b) prefetch aggressive, (c) raise staging to 256M, (d) tenant-prioritized eviction? small matrix.
Anya: I'm on it. posted preliminary matrix: prefetch-aggr + staging=256M gives best tail but ~7% more GPU usage. tenant-prio eviction reduces cross-tenant tail but increases overall eviction churn.
ci-bot: loadtest finished — 30m run, 95th latency baseline=120ms, prefetch-aggr+256M=160ms? wait, anomaly in the logs.
Olivia: can you upload the condensed flame/traces? quick pointer to what we should change in the allocator vs routing layer.
Anya: TLDR: root cause is two-fold: (1) small-slab fragmentation causing many hostpage fetches per request; (2) the offload admission doesn't account for microburst concurrency, so we let too many concurrent host reads in.
Mike: tradeoffs: tighten admission (reduce concurrent host reads) -> lowers tail but increases rejected/busy responses or longer queuing; aggressive prefetch -> lowers tail but raises memory cost; defrag/refactor allocator -> longer-term fix.
Devon: for near-term, what about hybrid: per-tenant concurrency cap + short-lived aggressive prefetch for top-k hot slices? keeps cost bounded.
Sam: agree. also add a fast-path: if request length < X && kv-hit -> skip host fetch entirely. small optimization but low-hanging.
Anya: I can prototype per-tenant concurrency limiter + small prefetch window (256KB per active tenant) and run the sweep.
Olivia: schedule a short canary run on dedicated pool after prototype. watch P99 and cost delta.
Mike: long-term RFC: slab compaction + async defrag task that runs during idle windows. we should propose an API for compaction hints in allocator.
Anya: noted. I'll file a short RFC draft: compaction worker + allocator hint API + admission caps.
Sam: also add sim harness tests for tenant-mix and fragmentation seeds so we don't regress.
Anya: will add seeds + fault-inject host-latency scenarios. planning to push PR with tests tomorrow.
Devon: thanks — this is a good path. small immediate mitigation + long-term allocator work. :+1:
ci-bot: ticket created: RNW-3589 (allocator-concurrency-prefetch-probe).
